question: Which of following is NOT a part of the Dravidian language family's four largest languages?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanskrit**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sanskrit** is **not a part of the Dravidian language family's** four largest languages.
 
• The four largest Dravidian languages are **Malayalam, Tamil, Kannada, and Telugu**.
 
• The Dravidian languages are predominantly spoken in Southern India and parts of Eastern and Central India.
 
• Sanskrit, on the other hand, is an ancient **Indo-Aryan language** and not related to the Dravidian language family.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sanskrit** is one of the oldest languages in the world and has a rich literary tradition.
 
• It is the classical language of ancient Indian scriptures, including the Vedas and Upanishads.
 
• Sanskrit has influenced many modern Indian languages, but it is not classified under the Dravidian language family.
 
• The Dravidian languages have their own distinct history and development, separate from the Indo-Aryan languages like Sanskrit.
 
• Efforts have been made to revive and preserve Sanskrit, given its cultural and historical significance.
